question: What will be the ending value of the UST 10Y Yield for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)

calls.reasoning: Random-walk anchor at the current level: DGS10 was 4.90 on Nov 4 and about 4.86-4.88 intraday on Nov 6, after strong October payrolls (+165k vs ~65k expected). The yield is down ~44bp from its 5.31 peak on Oct 5. Oct CPI on Nov 10 falls inside the window. Volatility has been high lately (two-week moves of 15-30bp), so the spread is set to an SD of ~17bp with no directional drift: the up-pressure from strong jobs offsets the recent downtrend momentum. Kalshi only has daily/monthly 10Y high/low contracts that don't match this close, and I found no matching Polymarket or Manifold market. Leaving the 4.255-6.255 range would need a move of more than 60bp in two weeks, so I declared no escape mass.

- CNBC 2026-11-05/06: the 10Y fell to about 4.84 on Nov 5 on a tech-stock selloff and a flight to safety. Democratic midterm gains eased Iran-escalation concerns and oil fell. Jobless claims came in at 189k.
- TradingEconomics 2026-11-06: the 10Y was at 4.86-4.88 (+2 to +4bp on the day) after October nonfarm payrolls of +165k vs ~65k expected, with unemployment down and wages above expectations. Down 44bp over 1 month; up ~75bp over 12 months. TE's Q4 model forecast is 4.89.
- Upcoming in the window: October CPI on Tue Nov 10, 8:30 ET (cpichart.com). Reportedly it will have no headline YoY figure.
- Status quo: the last observed level is about 4.86-4.90.
- Realized dispersion: 10-trading-day changes since September were about +28, +17, -15 and -23bp; August windows moved only about ±5bp. That implies an SD of roughly 15-20bp in the current regime.
- Resolves off the FRED DGS10 value initially published for Fri Nov 20, 2026, not intraday quotes from CNBC or TradingEconomics.
- Event window: Nov 9 -> Nov 20 close per the criteria. As of Nov 6, 0% has elapsed and 10 trading days remain.
- Markets: Kalshi has daily/monthly 10Y high/low contracts that don't match a Nov 20 close. No Polymarket or Manifold market was found.
- Searched for but not found: a Fed meeting date inside the window, and the size of the Treasury refunding auctions.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: last FRED print 4.90 (Nov 4), ~4.86-4.88 on Nov 6, Oct peak 5.31, strong Oct NFP, Dec hike odds ~76%, CPI in the window, no matching market. The only factual differences were the exact CPI date (Run 1 says Nov 10; the others couldn't confirm it) and small differences in how each run computed the spread. Neither matters for a Nov 20 close. I carried forward the shared random-walk center at ~4.87 and the ~17bp 10-day SD, which I agree with. No web access on this run.
